proposed_tolerance.mu_0ts: Same shape (99, 50, 3) and dtype float32; numpy.array_equal is what was observed. For the wrapper test use max |difference| <= 1e-6 (absolute; all values lie in [-1, 1], so this is about 17 float32 ulp for magnitudes in [0.5, 1)).
proposed_tolerance.final_reward: Printed string equal to `1.56e+00`; as a numeric check |difference| <= 0.005 (half a unit of the last printed digit).
proposed_tolerance.rollout_html: Exists, non-empty, starts with <!DOCTYPE html>, ends with </html>; byte equality (13083 bytes, same SHA-256) was observed and may be asserted on this machine.
proposed_tolerance.justification: The observed run-to-run difference is exactly zero in three executions, so there is no measured noise to size a looser tolerance from. A loose tolerance (for example 1e-3) would have no basis: in a contact-rich rollout that is re-weighted over 99 iterations, a genuine floating-point divergence does not stay small but grows to differences of the order of the values themselves, so the outcome is either bitwise agreement or a clearly visible mismatch. 1e-6 therefore only absorbs representation-level noise and makes a real divergence fail loudly instead of passing silently.
proposed_tolerance.scope_of_validity: Same machine, GPU (cuda:0, RTX 4070 Laptop, driver 581.04), interpreter and package set, same arguments, each run in a fresh process. Not established: CPU against GPU, another GPU or driver, another jax/brax build, or runs inside a long-lived process that has already compiled other programs. If the wrapper test ever shows a mismatch under these same conditions, treat it as a finding (GPU non-determinism appearing) and re-measure rather than widening the threshold.
proposed_tolerance.basis_strength: Three executions, two of them with a recorded exit status of 0.
